govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HockPaulFBIRele:
Paul L. Hoch kept an indexed list of FBI documents he received from the Assassination Information Bureau. The papers came from FBI file 62-109060, dating to 1963-64. His list was sent on January 12 and received on January 16, 1978, with columns for serial, page, date, and subject.

Researchers survived on lists like this one. Before digital files, an index with serial numbers was the map to a mountain of paper. Hoch's columns turn a stack of releases into something a scholar can search. The list preserves the bookkeeping that made assassination research possible, and it remains a finding aid to those releases.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-McIntireCarlRev:
The New York Times published a religion article profiling the Reverend Carl McIntire under the headline 'McIntire's Magic Touch.' McIntire was a fundamentalist leader in New Jersey. The article's joke is in its subheading sense: his touch, it says, turns to schism. Where McIntire led, churches split.

McIntire built a career on separation: from mainline churches, from rival fundamentalists, from former allies. A national paper explaining him to general readers had to cover both his following and his feuds. The profile preserves how the mainstream press presented a man who treated compromise as betrayal. It also marks his place in the religious fights of the postwar decades.
